channel.title: Breachfolio
channel.description: Practical cybersecurity guides, explained for people who need an answer tonight, not a glossary.

item.title: I clicked a phishing link: what actually happens now
item.description: If you only opened it and closed it, almost certainly nothing happened. What decides is what you did next: typed something, downloaded, or approved a prompt.

item.title: Is it safe to save passwords in your browser?
item.description: It does encrypt them, and anyone saying otherwise is out of date. What decides the risk is different: whether something can run on your computer as you.

item.title: A photo of your ID: what can really be done with it
item.description: The photo alone is rarely enough: what decides the risk is what else they hold about you. Plus the free credit check almost no article mentions.

item.title: Your data already leaked: how to check and what to do
item.description: How to check whether your email is in a breach, what appearing on the list actually means, and the order of actions that genuinely reduces your risk.

item.title: Android car screens infected through their own updater
item.description: Kaspersky documents the first malware built for Android car head units. It did not arrive through a dodgy app: it came through the unit’s own update channel.

item.title: vCenter flaw exploited five days after the patch
item.description: CVE-2026-59310 allows unauthenticated code execution on VMware vCenter. Broadcom patched on 29 July; exploitation began five days later. 361 victims in 47 countries.

item.title: Your website has been cloned: what to do
item.description: Someone copied your website to deceive your customers. How to gather evidence, which registrar and host to contact, and how to get it flagged in browsers.

item.title: Best VPN 2026: NordVPN vs Surfshark vs Proton VPN
item.description: NordVPN, Surfshark and Proton VPN compared on jurisdiction, audits, open source and what they actually protect. Two of the three are the same company.

item.title: Adobe patches a Magento flaw that hands over accounts
item.description: CVE-2026-71362 lets an attacker switch into another customer's session on Adobe Commerce, with no account and no clicking. Patch is out; Sansec reports attempts.

item.title: My email was hacked: what to do right now
item.description: Someone got into your email. Lock them out, undo the forwarding rule they left behind, and secure the accounts that reset through it, in that order.

item.title: Windows security event IDs: a triage cheat sheet
item.description: The Windows event IDs worth checking first when something looks wrong: sign-ins, privilege, new services, scheduled tasks and cleared logs.

item.title: Lab 06: test your detections with Atomic Red Team
item.description: Your home lab SIEM and IDS have never proved they detect anything. Run small, documented ATT&CK techniques with Atomic Red Team and find out which alerts fire.
